body: @carl-mastrangelo I think we will need to at least call `FindClass` and there is nothing we can do about this... Are you sure this is because of `FindClass` and not because we call `NetUtil.isIpV4StackPreferred()` ?

issue.title: Ensure we not run into classloading deadlocks while trying to load th…

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
…e native transports.

Motivation:

We used NetUtil.isIpV4StackPreferred() when loading JNI code which tries to load NetworkInterface in its static initializer. Unfortunally a lock on the NetworkInterface class init may be already hold somewhere else which may cause a loader deadlock.

Modifications:

Use Boolean.getBoolean("java.net.preferIPv4Stack")  to detect if ipv4 should be prefered.

Result:

Fixes [#7458].

body: @Scottmitch @carl-mastrangelo @ejona86 PTAL https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/7461 for a fix and some more details

agreed we should not load classes from JNI initialization that may get into class loading dead lock. [NativeStaticallyReferencedJniMethods](https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/4.1/transport-native-epoll/src/main/java/io/netty/channel/epoll/NativeStaticallyReferencedJniMethods.java) was created to avoid similar types of class loading issues.

@Scottmitch That approach I think is correct, but it wasn't clear to me how to make that change.  The epoll  code is constructing objects that can't exist in a staticly referenced only env.
